title: Retrospective Analysis of Clinical Outcomes Following Treatment with the Sentio Bone Conduction Implant in Pediatric Patients
summary:
Children with conductive hearing loss may experience difficulties hearing because sound cannot be adequately transmitted through the outer ear canal and middle ear to the inner ear. Bone conduction implants can provide an option to improve hearing in these cases. They transmit sound through the skull bone directly to the inner ear.

This study aims to investigate how well the new Sentio implant can be used in children. In particular, the study will assess whether hearing improves, whether complications occur during or after surgery, and whether implantation can be performed safely and effectively while taking the individual anatomy of each child into account.

For this purpose, data from all school-aged children who received a Sentio implant at our institution between August 2024 and August 2026 will be retrospectively analyzed. The evaluation will include, among other parameters, hearing test results before and after surgery and any complications that may have occurred.
conditions: Mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss, unspecified

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all school-aged patients who underwent implantation of a newactive bone conduction implant between August 2024 and August 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Implanted Sentio implant
•	Implantation performed at University Hospital Halle (Saale)
•	Age <14 years at the time of implantation
Exclusion criteria:
•	Failure to meet the inclusion criteria
•	No consent to participate in the study
